ecological_question: under what pond conditions does adult breeding effort cease to translate into downstream larval or metamorph production?

ecological_hypotheses.H1_baseline_coupling: within a species, greater seasonal calling-male abundance is associated with greater downstream larval production when habitat permits successful development
ecological_hypotheses.H2_context_dependence: the adult-to-larva relationship changes with pond conditions rather than being a fixed conversion across sites and years
ecological_hypotheses.H3_stage_specificity: if metamorph data are structurally adequate, environmental effects on adult-to-metamorph conversion can differ from effects on adult-to-larva conversion
ecological_hypotheses.H4_species_heterogeneity: Hyla arborea and Pelobates fuscus can differ in the habitat conditions that weaken breeding-to-offspring conversion
ecological_hypotheses.H5_external_recurrence: a broad claim requires recurrence in PINK, Mohonk, or another independent monitoring programme

prior_art_boundary.citation: Greenberg CH, Zarnoch SJ, Austin JD. 2017. Ecosphere 8:e01789. DOI 10.1002/ecs2.1789
prior_art_boundary.cannot_claim: first evidence that breeding effort and later reproductive output can be weakly coupled
prior_art_boundary.target_novelty: same-programme stage conversion localized to explicit adult and downstream protocols, habitat context, species heterogeneity, and independent recurrence
